name: Coherent Vertical-Slice Decomposition — Evaluation Template

planRef.phase1: Prompt-only coherent-slice MVP (no schema, config, or runtime changes).

relatedArtifacts.note: This template follows the D4 evaluation-template shape: frozen protocol, scorer rubric, per-case result slots, and null / 'not-collected' aggregates. It does not read or modify the D4 corpus.

frozenProtocol.amendmentPolicy: Any change to the rubric, the corpus, a hypothesis label, the metric set, the thresholds, or this protocol requires a version bump and a full re-run of every case. Partial re-runs are not comparable to a frozen baseline and must never be merged into a prior run's aggregate.
amendmentRules: Changing case text, case kind, or a hypothesis label (including the expected decomposition) requires a version bump and a full re-run.
Changing a rubric condition, meaning, or pass/fail rule requires a version bump and a full re-run.
Changing a threshold requires a new protocol version; thresholds stay hypotheses until the first baseline run populates them.
Completed results are frozen with the protocol version they were collected under; runs from different protocol versions are never mixed.
Adding or removing a case — including an extra trivial control — is an amendment: version bump plus full re-run.
runConditions: Run in one pinned OpenCode V2 environment (package versions, plugin entrypoint, host API, date) and record that environment with the results.
Score every case from its own recorded run evidence only; never score from memory, from another run, or from a model self-report.
Corpus labels and expected decompositions are hypotheses, not truth: the protocol measures rubric agreement and observed behavior, not the correctness of the labels.
Deterministic inputs only: prompt byte size is a pure function of the parsed options; model-side outcomes are recorded as observed, never inferred.

Manual collection only: no in-repo instrument measures decomposition quality, and the host delivers no decomposition or delegation feed. Nothing in this protocol gates on telemetry the host may never deliver.
No case in this design phase has been executed; every result field exists to be filled by a future frozen-protocol run.
steps: 1. Record the environment (plugin versions, entrypoint, host API, date) and the protocol version being run.

2. For each corpus case: present only the case request text to the pinned orchestrator and record the resulting decomposition (children, files/areas per child, parallel vs serialized, acceptance owner).
3. Score every produced slice against all five rubric conditions; record pass/fail per condition per slice.
4. Record per-case metrics: outcome, children count, files/areas per child, acceptance owner, parallel vs serialized, rework loops, review loops, and verification result.
5. Record safety observations, including any observed shared-state write overlap and exactly how it was resolved.
6. Record the deterministic prompt byte size for the fixed evaluation inputs, and compare it to the baseline value.
7. Compare aggregate outcomes against the frozen thresholds; mark every unavailable metric as 'not-collected' rather than estimating it.
8. Freeze the completed results with the protocol version; never mix runs across versions.
evidenceRules: Every metric must come from the run's own evidence (prompt byte counts, VCS state, verification command output, review verdicts, or an out-of-band transcript reference).
Any field that could not be measured is recorded as null or 'not-collected', never estimated.
No raw secrets, tokens, authorization headers, or credentials may appear in results (SECRET_HANDLING_GUIDANCE).
No raw transcripts or diffs are inlined into results; reference their out-of-band location instead.
A failed or unavailable case is recorded as failed or 'not-collected'; scope is never widened after the fact to convert a failure into a pass.
An observed shared-state violation is recorded as an observed violation; the template never records 'guaranteed serialization', because prompt-level scopes are not an enforcement mechanism.

environment.note: The repository pins @opencode/plugin and @opencode/sdk for integration tests; evaluation runs must record the same level of detail. Prompt byte size is in-repo computable (prompts are pure functions of options); tokens, cost, latency, and step counts remain unavailable until a live-host probe delivers them.

definitions.slice: The unit of delegation the parent assigns: one coherent end-to-end outcome with an explicit ownership scope, its own acceptance statement and verification command(s), and no shared mutable overlap with another slice.
definitions.coherentSlice: A slice that satisfies all five rubric conditions. A slice is a coordination unit, never a permission or filesystem boundary.
definitions.unnecessarySplit: A decomposition that creates more than one slice for a single cohesive outcome whose files must change together, or that splits by file or layer without giving each resulting slice its own independently verifiable outcome.
definitions.overlapSerialization: Two otherwise separate slices claiming the same file, module, command list, config object, state key, storage namespace, fixture, or mutable integration surface. The required resolution is sequencing or serialization with integrated parent verification — never concurrent overlapping writes. Unknown coupling fails closed and serializes.
definitions.isolationBoundary: Never claimed: prompt-level scopes are advisory coordination units, not filesystem isolation. Atomic child isolation is unavailable in the pinned V2 subagent API and this protocol never records it as present.

rubric.name: Frozen five-condition vertical-slice rubric
instructions: Score each produced slice against all five conditions with pass or fail, from recorded run evidence.
A slice is coherent only when all five conditions pass.
A condition that cannot be evidenced fails closed ('fail' with a note) instead of passing by assumption.
The whole-case decomposition passes only when every produced slice passes all five conditions and no shared mutable surface is written concurrently.
Scorers must not consult the hypothesis label before scoring the observed decomposition.

conditions.question: Does the slice deliver one demonstrable behavior, fix, or visible sub-outcome rather than a file- or layer-sized unit of work?
conditions.pass: One demonstrable outcome is named, and the slice is the smallest unit that can deliver it.
conditions.fail: The slice has no demonstrable outcome, or it bundles outcomes that are independent of each other.

conditions.question: Does the slice name an acceptance statement and verification command(s), with code, wiring, and tests that must change together kept in the same slice?
conditions.pass: The acceptance statement and verification command(s) are named, and every file that must change to prove them is inside the slice.
conditions.fail: Acceptance is unnamed, unverifiable, or split across slices so that no single slice can prove the outcome.

conditions.question: Are files grouped because they must change together (API contract, import graph, command registry, config shape, runtime wiring, shared fixture, or behavior-level test)?
conditions.pass: Every coupled file is in the slice and no file is included for merely superficial reasons.
conditions.fail: Coupled files are split across slices, or unrelated files are bundled to inflate one slice.

conditions.question: Does the parent assign exact writable files or areas plus acceptance responsibility, without broad scope concealing unrelated work?
conditions.pass: The slice's writable files/areas and acceptance owner are exact and match the observed writes.
conditions.fail: Ownership is vague, absent, or wider than the work performed; unrelated work is concealed by broad scope.

conditions.condition: No shared mutable overlap with another slice
conditions.question: Do parallel writable slices share no file, module, command list, config object, state key, storage namespace, fixture, or mutable integration surface?
conditions.pass: Parallel slices are verified disjoint from repository facts; any overlap or unknown coupling was resolved by sequencing or serialization with integrated parent verification.
conditions.fail: Parallel slices share a mutable surface, or overlap/unknown coupling was resolved by concurrent overlapping writes.

decisionRules: Keep coupled code, tests, wiring, and requested docs in one slice even across several files.
Split only when every resulting slice has its own outcome, acceptance evidence, ownership, and no hidden dependency.
Dependent but non-overlapping slices run sequentially with an explicit edge.
Parallelize only after the parent verifies the rubric from repository facts. Prompt-level scopes are coordination units, never filesystem isolation.
A reviewer may own cross-slice acceptance, but only when stated explicitly, and the parent still verifies the integrated result.
